scenes.title: SELECT
scenes.narration: SELECT is the workhorse of SQL, the clause you use to read and shape data out of a table.

scenes.title: What SELECT does
bullets: Names the columns you want returned
Pairs with FROM to choose the source
scenes.narration: SELECT lists exactly which columns you want in the result, so you retrieve only what you need. It can also compute expressions and rename outputs with aliases for clarity. It always works alongside FROM, which points to the table the data comes from.

scenes.heading: Explicit columns vs SELECT *
scenes.narration: Listing explicit columns keeps queries lean, moving only the data you actually use. SELECT star grabs every column, which is convenient for exploring but wasteful in production. It also makes results brittle, since adding a column silently changes the output.

scenes.title: Selecting specific columns
scenes.code:
SELECT first_name, last_name, email
FROM customers;
scenes.narration: This query asks for just three columns from the customers table. By naming them explicitly, we avoid pulling unneeded data across the network. The result is a tidy list of names and emails, one row per customer.

scenes.text: Select only the columns you need, and SELECT becomes both efficient and self-documenting.
scenes.narration: Reach for explicit column lists over SELECT star, and your queries stay efficient and clear about their intent.
